outcome: Instruction text such as 'can't be countered' on a triggered ability applies while it is on the stack, so a counter attempt does nothing to it.
An ability with several trigger conditions and an 'all of those conditions' instruction checks whether every condition occurred in the period, regardless of whether it triggered from them.
An ability triggers automatically when a game event or state matches its trigger event, and does nothing yet.
A triggered ability triggers even when casting spells or activating abilities is not legal or is precluded by an effect.
All abilities that trigger 'at the beginning of' a phase or step trigger when it begins.
An ability triggers once per occurrence of its trigger event, and once per occurrence when one event contains several, such as one trigger per land destroyed by a single spell.
An effect stating a triggered ability triggers additional times makes it trigger that many times in total, without applying to itself or to delayed and reflexive abilities.
A 'becomes' trigger fires only when the named change happens, not when the state already exists, and a 'becomes tapped' ability does not fire for a permanent entering tapped.
A triggered ability whose source is never visible to all players does not trigger.
note: hidden-zone sources are rare in practice

outcome: An ability does not trigger when its trigger event is prevented or replaced, such as damage fully prevented.
An ability marked 'Do this only once each turn' triggers only if its controller has not yet taken that action this turn.
A triggered ability goes on the stack the next time a player would receive priority, as the topmost object, with only the ability's text.
A triggered ability is controlled by whoever controlled its source when it triggered.

note: controller orders simultaneous triggers; the APNAP structure is a procedure over choices

outcome: A modal triggered ability with no choosable mode is removed from the stack.
note: announcing the mode is a decision, removal when no mode is legal is the outcome

outcome: A triggered ability for which no legal choices (such as targets) can be made is removed from the stack without resolving.
An intervening-if ability triggers only if its condition holds when the event occurs, and is removed from the stack doing nothing if the condition is false on resolution.
An optional or 'unless' triggered ability goes on the stack regardless, and the choice or the unless-clause is dealt with on resolution.
A zone-change trigger's effect acts on the object in the zone it moved to, and does nothing to it if it cannot be found there, including if it left and returned.
Enters-the-battlefield abilities of all permanents on the battlefield, including the newcomers, are checked when permanents enter and trigger on a match.

Continuous effects apply to a permanent from the moment it enters, so a creature under 'lose all abilities' does not trigger its own enters ability, and a land made a creature triggers creature-enters abilities.
Leaves-the-battlefield abilities trigger when a permanent moves from the battlefield to another zone, and acting on the card checks only the first zone it went to.
'Enters with', 'as enters', 'enters as' and 'enters tapped' are static abilities applied as part of the entering event and do not use the stack.
An Aura's trigger on the enchanted permanent leaving can find that permanent's new object in its new zone and the Aura's new object in the graveyard after state-based actions.
An effect creates a delayed triggered ability that triggers later when its event occurs.
A delayed triggered ability triggers only if its event occurs after it was created, so an event before the creating effect resolves does not trigger it.
A delayed triggered ability triggers once, on the next occurrence of its event, unless it has a stated duration such as 'this turn'.
A delayed triggered ability affects its referenced object even if its characteristics changed, but does nothing if the object left the expected zone, including leaving and returning.
A delayed triggered ability created by a spell has that spell as its source and is controlled by the spell's controller on resolution.
A delayed triggered ability created by an ability has the same source and is controlled by that ability's controller on resolution.
A delayed trigger created through a static ability's replacement effect has that object as source and is controlled by its controller when the replacement applied.
A delayed trigger created when a player takes an action allowed by a static ability has that object as source and is controlled by its controller at the time of the action.
A delayed trigger that counts resolutions of its creating ability in a turn is created only once, on the appropriate resolution.
A state trigger triggers as soon as the game state matches and does not trigger again until it has left the stack, then retriggers if the state still matches.

note: in a two-player game the first loss ends the game, so a trigger on a player losing never goes on the stack

outcome: Looking-back-in-time triggers use the abilities and object appearance immediately before the event rather than after it.
Leaves-the-battlefield, sacrifice, leaves-graveyard and visible-to-hand/library triggers look back in time, so an artifact destroyed simultaneously with creatures still triggers on their deaths.
Abilities that trigger when a permanent phases out look back in time.
Abilities that trigger when an object becomes unattached look back in time.
Abilities that trigger when a player loses control of an object look back in time.
Abilities that trigger when a spell is countered look back in time.

note: in a two-player game the first loss ends the game, so a trigger on a player losing never goes on the stack

describes how linked static and triggered abilities are written on objects

outcome: A reflexive triggered ability triggers only if the stated action occurred during the creating resolution, such as the sacrifice for Heart-Piercer Manticore.
A reflexive trigger triggers once per occurrence of its event during the resolution, except it triggers once when a cost was paid multiple times.
